title: When AI Benchmarks Plateau: A Systematic Study of Benchmark Saturation
metric_proposed: saturation rate and effect of benchmark age
how_we_operationalize: Benchmark-health reporting: we compute a local ceiling rate (share of items solved correctly on every repeat) and treat it as a saturation signal, following the paper's finding that saturation rises with age and is not fixed by public-data redesign alone.
limitations: It measures suite-level saturation, not item validity; with 60 items our ceiling rate is a small-sample estimate and cannot establish that a benchmark is saturated in their sense.

title: Nine Judges, Two Effective Votes: Correlated Errors Undermine LLM Evaluation Panels
reference_standard: human annotations (100 per item) on three NLI datasets
metric_proposed: Kish effective sample size and panel accuracy gap
how_we_operationalize: Grounds the cross-family judge design: treat N judges as at most a handful of independent votes and report both-wrong rates rather than assuming independence; effective-panel-size analysis is future work.
limitations: Their nine judges are NLI models over seven families, not medical rubric judges; the two-effective-votes figure does not transfer as a number to our panel.

title: JEV-as-a-Judge: Accept When Confident, Escalate When Unsure
reference_standard: blinded human adjudication against sixteen judges
metric_proposed: accuracy at matched cost; escalation rate
how_we_operationalize: Informs the confidence fields and a future two-tier judge: accept confident verdicts, escalate the rest, and freeze the threshold in advance on held-out pairs instead of trusting a published cutoff.
limitations: Routing gains weaken on style-adversarial and reference-free prose; our medical free text is closer to that hard end, and no escalation tier is implemented in v0.1.

title: SkillsBench: Benchmarking How Well Agent Skills Work Across Diverse Tasks
how_we_operationalize: Method template for paired experiments: we compare judges and rules as matched-pair deltas on the same items, as this benchmark does for with/without-Skill runs.
limitations: Its 87 agentic tasks have deterministic verifiers; medical free text has no deterministic pass condition, so paired deltas here are judge-verdict deltas, not pass-rate gains.

title: Agent-as-a-Judge
how_we_operationalize: Future-work context only: it maps tool-using and trajectory-checking judges, none of which v0.1 runs.
limitations: A survey, not an experiment; it asserts greater verifiability for agentic judges but provides no number we can operationalise.

title: Claw-Eval: Towards Trustworthy Evaluation of Autonomous Agents
reference_standard: human-verified rubric items; execution traces, audit logs and environment snapshots
metric_proposed: Completion, Safety and Robustness with Pass@k and Pass^k
how_we_operationalize: Future-work reference for trace-grounded grading: it records execution traces and audit logs so outcomes can be checked after the fact, the model for a future trace-level task type.
limitations: Its 300 tasks are software-agent workflows, and the trace channels it relies on do not exist in our text-only v0.1 runs.

title: The Art of Building Verifiers for Computer Use Agents
reference_standard: process and outcome human labels on CUAVerifierBench
metric_proposed: separate process and outcome rewards; failure taxonomy
how_we_operationalize: Separates path from endpoint in our rubric: reasoning_soundness scores the reasoning path while diagnostic_accuracy and management_appropriateness score the endpoint, so a right answer by a wrong path does not score full marks.
limitations: Evidence comes from web-agent trajectories with screenshots; the process/outcome split is sensible for our text rubric but has not been tested on medical prose.

title: Terminal-Bench: Benchmarking Agents on Hard, Realistic Tasks in Command Line Interfaces
how_we_operationalize: Future-work reference for hard, environment-backed tasks with per-task tests; no terminal or executable task type exists in v0.1.
limitations: Terminal environments are far from medical vignettes; only the hard-task-plus-verification design is transferable.

title: PostTrainBench: Can LLM Agents Automate LLM Post-Training?
reference_standard: held-out benchmark score under bounded compute
how_we_operationalize: Informs the leakage and reward-hacking risk note: it lets agents optimise directly against a scored target, which is exactly the optimisation pressure we screen for when a model improves on our own items.
limitations: Its compute-bounded post-training setting is not our judge pipeline; it supplies a risk model, not a measured leakage result for this repository.

title: LifeVal: Evaluating AI Model Performance on Personalized Agentic Consumer Tasks
reference_standard: task-creator rubrics with real personal context
how_we_operationalize: Future-work reference for longitudinal, personalized context: it builds tasks from real conversations, memories and personal files, the direction we would need to test context retention over time.
limitations: Consumer tasks are not clinical, willingness-to-pay weighting does not transfer, and no longitudinal time series is used in v0.1.

title: Same Verdict, Different Reasons: LLM-as-a-Judge and Clinician Disagreement on Medical Chatbot Completeness
metric_proposed: AUC for incomplete-response detection and explanation agreement
how_we_operationalize: Informs the completeness criterion and its limitations: verdict agreement does not mean the same reason, so we do not treat completeness judge scores as clinician-equivalent.
limitations: It covers completeness only and finds near-chance discrimination for several judge/rubric combinations; it does not validate our anchors.

title: Evaluating medical AI under missing information: same-provider judges and human raters change apparent safety
reference_standard: four-provider judge panel plus blinded clinician anchor
metric_proposed: same-provider judge association after leniency adjustment; Fleiss kappa
how_we_operationalize: Informs the self-preference and same-family risk note: judge identity changes apparent safety, so we record the judge provider with every number and do not use a model family to judge its own outputs.
limitations: The same-provider effect is measured on truncated HealthBench conversations with a 50-item clinician subsample; the effect size is not transferable, only the warning.

title: Evaluating Large Language Model Raters for German Open-Response Clinical Questions: A Physician-Annotated Benchmark Study of Agreement, Evaluator Bias, and Abstention
task: LLM rater validation on open-response clinical questions
metric_proposed: Cohen kappa, evaluator alignment, self and intra-family bias, abstention
how_we_operationalize: Benchmark-design reference for validating a rater against physicians rather than against another judge: we report agreement with n and never call a judge clinician-level without a blinded human reference.
limitations: The benchmark is German and single-specialty; its bias findings motivate our caveats but do not validate any English judge we might use.

title: Can LLMs Accurately Score Medical Diagnoses and Clinical Reasoning?
task: diagnosis and reasoning scoring by an LLM jury
reference_standard: expert clinician panel plus independent re-scoring panel
metric_proposed: error metrics, agreement, severe-risk errors, isotonic calibration
how_we_operationalize: Informs the jury-score calibration caveat: an uncalibrated LLM jury is systematically offset from clinician panels, so we report jury scores as ordinal comparisons and leave calibration as future work.
limitations: It scores diagnoses in LMIC hospital cases, not rubric-graded response quality, and the isotonic calibration it finds useful is not implemented here.

title: Capabilities of Gemini Models in Medicine
reference_standard: 14 medical benchmarks; clinician relabeling of MedQA
how_we_operationalize: External precedent for key-noise screening: its clinician relabeling of MedQA reported roughly 4% unanswerable items and roughly 3% labeling errors, which is why our audit reports key correctness as unknown rather than zero.
limitations: Its relabeling is its own clinicians on the MedQA test split, not on the split we audit; the 7% figure is a precedent, not a measurement of our items.

title: Medmarks: A Comprehensive Open-Source LLM Benchmark Suite for Medical Tasks
reference_standard: 30 benchmarks with verifiable metrics and LLM-as-a-judge
metric_proposed: suite-level accuracy and answer-order bias probe
how_we_operationalize: Benchmark-quality reference: it treats saturation and answer-order bias as suite properties to measure, which is why our benchmark-health reporting includes ceiling and order checks next to accuracy.
limitations: A model-ranking suite evaluation, not a validation of any single criterion; its rankings are time-bound and are not evidence for our rubric.

title: How to Run Statistics over LLM Judges and Trust the Results: Calibrated Inference for Small-Sample AI Evaluation with evalstats
metric_proposed: calibrated confidence intervals and false-positive control
how_we_operationalize: Informs our small-n statistics caveat: raw tests over judge scores can inflate false positives, so we report intervals with n and label comparisons exploratory; PPI correction is not implemented.
limitations: PPI needs a human-labelled calibration set we do not have; applying it is future work, so our intervals remain uncalibrated for judge bias.

title: Position: Don't Use the CLT in LLM Evals With Fewer Than a Few Hundred Datapoints
task: uncertainty quantification for small LLM benchmarks
reference_standard: position paper; frequentist and Bayesian alternatives
how_we_operationalize: Justifies our interval choice: at n in the tens we report bootstrap or Wilson intervals instead of CLT normal-approximation intervals, which this position paper shows understate uncertainty.
limitations: A position paper with recommendations, not a coverage proof for our bootstrap; our BCa variant is itself unvalidated against a coverage simulation (see G3).

title: Benchmark Integrity and Reasoning-Trace Errors in Medical Question Answering With Large Language Models: Mixed Methods Study With Sparse Autoencoders
task: MedQA benchmark integrity and reasoning traces
how_we_operationalize: Related-work support for key-noise and trace screening: it reports benchmark-integrity and reasoning-trace errors in medical QA, which is the concern behind treating our key correctness as unassessed rather than clean.
limitations: Only its Crossref title was confirmed (the DOI resolves to an accepted JMIR preprint; no abstract was read), so no specific number or method from it is used here.
